version: t2-past v10.1, 9 November 2026, parse_date fix for a US month-first n/n/yyyy date (10/30/2026 style) that used to crash the run; otherwise unchanged from t2-past v10
industry: Australian residential construction (home building). Generic; not tied to any past client.
columns: Why it matters to your portfolio
one_sentence: Why it matters to your portfolio

window.note: Past week: seven days to Sunday 1 November 2026, the scan date the case file gives as today. Run on 8 November 2026.

P1.stale_from_prior: The addendum holds one stale item per row of the case's last week's list, plus older stories a scan may re-report, each with id, urls, topic and period.

P2.case: case-t2/past-2.txt (made from past-week 1 run 1's table, as case-t2/week-b.md describes for week B)

window.note: Past week: seven days to Sunday 8 November 2026, the scan date the case file gives as today. Run on 8 November 2026.

P2.stale_from_prior: The addendum holds one stale item per row of the past-week 1 run 1 table, plus older stories, each with id, urls, topic and period.

addendum_rule: News is live, so a week's stories cannot be known on 7 November. Before the first run of a week, a key writer who does not tune the prompt scans the week, and writes and commits the addendum alone, with its time to the second in rounds-t2/PREREG.md. The addendum holds: stories (as tier 1: id, must, what, urls, match, evidence url, quote and date, each evidence checked by rnd/check_urls.py and its page text saved for offline re-scoring), echo clusters (one story id with every outlet URL found, at least the press release and its echoes), and for week B the stale items from the week A list (each with id, urls as a list, topic and period). For each must story, the key writer confirms when writing the addendum that the evidence page carries a metadata date (published-time meta, JSON-LD datePublished or <time datetime>) or, failing that, a stated release date in its text as the T1 pass describes, and records page_date_source: "page metadata" or "page text" in that story's evidence. A must story's what and evidence quote must not match a stale item by topic and period. score_industry.py refuses to score a week whose addendum is missing, not tracked by git, has a malformed stale item, or breaks either must-story rule, and records the addendum's commit time in the score. The 'nothing material' line can only be tested if the key writer finds a quiet week; if the addendum lists no story, a correct run writes that line.

traps.what: A stale story re-reported as new: the row's date or its page's own date is outside the window, or the row matches a stale item.
traps.pass: Every row's Date is in the window; its page's own date comes from page metadata (published-time meta, JSON-LD datePublished or <time datetime>), or, only when the page has no metadata date, from the page's own first stated date in its text (a labelled date such as 'Released 30/10/2026' or 'Published 29 October 2026', never 'Next Release'; else the first standalone yyyy-mm-dd date), and is in the window, within one day of the row's Date; and no row matches a stale item by URL prefix, or by its topic AND its period pattern. A row that matches a stale topic but no period is listed for review, not failed. The row's own date text is never searched for on the page.

traps.what: A press release echoed by several outlets is counted once.
traps.pass: No two rows map to the same addendum story or echo cluster (URL first, then match pattern).
At most max_rows rows, and every row passes R1 and T1.

rules.R1: Every row's Source URL passes rnd/check_urls.py (HTTP 200, no soft 404, page holds the quote) and the quote is max_quote_words words or fewer. Critical.
rules.S1: Why it matters to us and Quote are each one sentence (the prompt's own rule; a tier-1 gap).
rules.K1: Every must story in the week's addendum is reported, industry and AI alike, matched by URL then pattern, never by Type label.
rules.F1: The table has exactly the key's columns, Type is industry or AI, every row has a parseable date. A type with no row labelled with it has the line 'Nothing material this week: <type>'; a type with a row has no such line (by Copilot's own labels: a format check). With no table, both lines are present.
rules.C1: Caps: at most type_caps['industry'] industry rows and type_caps['AI'] AI rows. A row on a key story counts under the key's tag; a story tagged both, or a row no story matched, counts under Copilot's own Type label. Copilot's label never decides which story a row matches, so a story that fits both types cannot break the caps. Critical.
rules.PA1: Portfolio: a row on a key story that lists areas names at least one of THAT story's expected areas in Why it matters to your portfolio (exact words, case and white space ignored). Any other area name does not pass. Every must story lists areas, each an exact item of the profile fixture's Portfolio list.
rules.A2: Action is None, or names who acts: a Leadership team role from the profile fixture, or the executive ('You ...' at the start).

closed_gaps: From industry/rounds/README.md 'Known latent scorer gaps': (i) stale items need topic AND period, no single-token anchor; (ii) a page's date must come from its metadata, never from the row's own date text found on the page; (iii) each window is exactly seven days including the run day; (iv) one-sentence Why and Quote are scored (S1); (v) committed output redacts a real name in display text only, never inside a URL, so it stays re-scorable; the unredacted copy goes to the gitignored artefacts folder; (vi) no real company or person is a match pattern.
pass: Three fresh-chat runs per week, each scored with score_industry.py --key answer-key-t2-past-v10.json --week P1 (or P2). Malformed output fails. Otherwise pass needs T1, T2, T3, R1, S1, K1, F1, C1, PA1 and A2. One critical failure fails the round. Both weeks, all three runs each, must pass; then holdout-past-2 v2 3 of 3.
counter_metric: Items reported per type (padding: counter_metric.items_by_type) and must stories found per type (counter_metric.must_found_by_type). So-what and action quality are the reader's check, not scored.
ruler_change: Approved by the owner on 8 November 2026: two past weeks replace the live weeks of 16 and 23 November 2026, so the kit can be built on 8 November. Each case file states its scan date as today; prompt v1 is unchanged. Not comparable with the live-week plan in answer-key-t2.json.
key_change: t2-past v10.1, 9 November 2026 (ticket 31, score_industry.py fix, not a key change): parse_date read every n/n/yyyy date as day/month, so a US month-first date with the day over 12 (such as a page metadata date 10/30/2026, meaning 30 October) raised ValueError that __main__ did not catch, and the run got no score. v10.1: an n/n/yyyy date reads month/day only when the second field is over 12 and the first is 12 or under, the one unambiguous reading; both fields 12 or under still default to day/month (Australian), which stays a known limit on a genuinely ambiguous date; any date invalid under the chosen reading, or raised anywhere else in parse_date, now returns None instead of crashing. No column, trap, cap, portfolio area or pass rule changed. Not comparable with t2-past v10 for a run whose scorer crashed on this bug. Previous: t2-past v10, 8 November 2026 (ticket 29, SPEC-redesign section 6, ADR 0016 v): the scan adds up to three AI items beside up to five industry items, each with why it matters to the portfolio, so what and action. The addenda answer-key-t2-past-1-v10.json and answer-key-t2-past-2-v10.json copy the v8 addenda's industry stories and stale items unchanged, add a type tag and expected portfolio areas to each story, and add AI stories, AI echo clusters and AI stale items written by a separate key writer who saw no Copilot answer; load() refuses an addendum whose stories break the v8 one-story-per-pattern check across both types, a story with no valid type, a must story with no areas, an area that is not a portfolio item of the profile fixture case-t2/profile.md, or a profile fixture that is uncommitted or edited. Not comparable with any earlier round. Previous: t2-past v8, 8 November 2026 (one documented key fault, round 'v5 on t2-past v7', rounds-t2/PREREG.md, known item i). Run t2-v5k7-p1-1 failed T2 because P1 story W3's match pattern, the bare stem 'affordab', also matched an unrelated row about 'social and affordable homes'. A separate key writer, who did not open prompts/, any run folder, any case file or any Copilot answer, reviewed every story match pattern in the P1 and P2 addenda and wrote answer-key-t2-past-1-v8.json and answer-key-t2-past-2-v8.json (only match fields changed; each file's match_review says why). Under story_match_exclusive, load() refuses an addendum where a story's pattern misses its own what and evidence quote or matches another story's. URLs, evidence, stale items, rules, traps and the pass rule are unchanged. Not comparable with t2-past v1 to v7 rounds. Previous: t2-past v7, 8 November 2026 (one documented scorer limit, round 'v5 on t2-past v6', rounds-t2/PREREG.md, known item i). Run t2-v5-p1-1 row 1 cited a page that builds its text by script: the fetch returned HTTP 200 and the quote sat only in an escaped data blob, and the Chrome-text route applied only to a page that refuses the script. v7 (chrome_text_on_miss): when the script fetch returns HTTP 200, the page is not a soft 404, and its text lacks the quote, the row is checked from the page's visible text captured in Chrome (<text-dir>/<sha1 of url>.txt); it passes only if that text holds the quote, and fails if the text is missing or only a challenge page. T1 is unchanged: a page the script fetched with HTTP 200 is dated from its own HTML by the v6 rules, never from the Chrome text, and a page with no metadata, labelled or date-line date has no page date and fails T1 (require_meta_date). Not comparable with t2-past v1 to v6 rounds. Previous: t2-past v6, 8 November 2026 (one documented scorer limit, round 'v4 on t2-past v5', rounds-t2/PREREG.md). Run t2-v4-p1-1 row 4 ended its quote with the citation chip [abcb.prod....bcb.gov.au]: a shortened domain whose ellipsis sits next to a dot. The v1.2 chip pattern joins label parts only by one dot, one '...' or one '…', so the chip stayed in the quote. v6 (chip_dot_run): any run of dots and ellipsis characters may join two label parts; a chip still holds only letters, digits, hyphens, dots and ellipses inside square brackets, so a tool marker such as web_open:<url> is never stripped. Everything else unchanged. Not comparable with t2-past v1 to v5 rounds. Previous: t2-past v5, 8 November 2026 (two documented scorer limits, Codex review after round 'v3 on t2-past v4', rounds-t2/PREREG.md). (a) score_industry.py knew a PDF only by its %PDF- prefix; v5 fetches with check_urls.fetch_raw and tests check_urls.is_pdf, the same Content-Type or prefix test check_urls.fetch() uses for quotes. (b) An XMP CreateDate that sits only in a compressed metadata stream was not read; v5 reads it from poppler's pdfinfo -meta, after the raw-bytes XMP search and only when no other date is found. Text rules, order of fallbacks and closed gap (ii) unchanged. Not comparable with t2-past v1 to v4 rounds. Previous: t2-past v4, 8 November 2026 (documented key gap, decided by the orchestrator after the network re-score under rounds-t2/PREREG.md 'Re-score result'). Run t2-v3k3-p1-1 row 5 cited a Victorian Government Gazette PDF that holds the quote and states 'Friday 30 October 2026' on its cover and '30 October 2026' on its own line, but t2-past v3 read the PDF's raw bytes and took the first yyyy-mm-dd, an embedded XMP date of 6 January 2011 from an old template. v4: a PDF's page date comes from its pdftotext text by the v2 and v3 text rules (labelled date, standalone yyyy-mm-dd, a line that holds only a day-month-year date). Only when the text gives no date: the document-info CreationDate, then the first embedded XMP CreateDate. Closed gap (ii) still holds. HTML pages are dated as in v3. Not comparable with t2-past v1, v2 or v3 rounds.
failure_cause: Every failed item carries cause: the types, by the key's tag, of the rows or stories that failed it. The score's failure_cause lists them, so each failed run is logged as an industry rule or an AI rule (SPEC-redesign section 6, pre-registered failure count).
legacy: Diagnostic only, decides nothing: --legacy reads an answer in the v9 columns as industry rows and scores only R1, T1, T2, T3 (five rows), S1, K1 (industry and both must stories) and F1.
